title: Dynamic scope rebalancing & launch cut-criteria runbook for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Create an operational runbook that defines dynamic scope rebalancing, cut criteria tiers, telemetry gates, and coordinated release notes handoff for the combined API / Console / Runtime release train. This ticket captures the decision matrix for automatic scope adjustments during the freeze window, the approved fallback behaviors for runtime model variants, and the cross-team communication plan for last-minute cut decisions. The goal is to enable an engineering-first, low-friction decision process that preserves customer SLAs while preventing scope creep during the 2-week launch runway.
acceptance_criteria: A single cut-criteria matrix is published and reviewed by ENG/Design/Sales/Support
Telemetry gates for canary and 25% rollout are defined and validated on the prod staging dashboard
Release-notes snippet template distributed to component owners; release-notes PR template created
Emergency rollback triggers and playbook steps documented and tested in a tabletop exercise
Owners for each tier and each component (API, Console, Runtime) are assigned and acknowledged
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff with ENG/Design/Console/Runtime; aligned on objective and timeline; Marcus to draft initial matrix
2026-03-11: Marcus submitted first cut-criteria draft; ENG request: add KV cache fallback behavior for high-latency paths
2026-03-12: Design reviewed UI-level impact for Console feature flags; suggested simplified copy for user-facing release notes
2026-03-13: QA outlined a 4-hour smoke window requirement for runtime deploys; added to gating criteria
2026-03-14: PM review complete; updated matrix to include canary telemetry SLOs and rollback thresholds
decisions: Adopt three-tier cut model: Tier 0 (must ship), Tier 1 (cuttable with fallback), Tier 2 (post-launch backlog)
Canary rollout policy: 5% for first 2 hours, 25% for next 24 hours if telemetry gates pass; full rollout after 72h
Fallback model behavior: runtime will automatically route to quantized model variant when 95th pct latency exceeds 1.2x SLO for over 10 min
Release notes will be consolidated into a single PR per component using the provided template; owners supply 2-line blurbs
Cut decisions during freeze: PM + ENG lead + release engineer must sign off; on-call SRE must acknowledge telemetry availability
review_feedback: SRE (Priya): Ensure we have synthetic traffic for pages served by Console before canary; otherwise deny canary
Design (Elena): Suggest removing feature-level screenshots from initial release notes to reduce last-minute assets
Engineering (Samir): Request separate rollback sequence for Runtime that preserves in-flight KV cache state
Support (Jordan): Need an internal-facing FAQ and severity classification for customer dials after rollout
rollout_plan: Phased rollout coordinated across teams: (1) deploy runtime in staging and run synthetic load for 24h, (2) canary at 5% for 2 hours with telemetry checks (error rate, p95, user-facing failures), (3) expand to 25% for 24h if gates pass, (4) enable Console flag for 25% and run UX smoke, (5) full rollout at 72h. Each step requires the release engineer to post gate results to the release channel and update the release-notes PR with status.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected latency spike in runtime under production traffic. Mitigation: Auto-fallback to quantized model variant and reduce batch size; trigger on-call and open SEV if spike persists > 15 minutes
Risk: Console regression causing navigation failures. Mitigation: Gate Console rollout with UX smoke tests; if failures > 0.5% of sessions, roll back to previous flag cohort
Risk: Release-notes mismatch across components. Mitigation: Single release-notes maintainer (PM) consolidates snippets and locks copy 24h before cut
notes_for_engineering: ENG: Implement runtime 'soft-cut' feature-flag that enables routing to fallback quantized model when latency gates trip. Add a bootstrap config to the deploy manifest that enables synthetic traffic endpoints for SRE during the staging window.
notes_for_design: Design: Prepare two variants of the Console banner (concise and expanded) depending on final scope; provide copy snippets for release notes and internal FAQ by 2026-03-24.
notes_for_go_to_market: GTM: Coordinate embargo timing with marketing and sales engineering; prepare a single public-facing bullet and a detailed partner briefing doc. Sales to receive 'What changed' 48 hours prior to public rollout.
